title: Weighted Time Interval Merger & Gap Analyzer
description: Implement two functions in `interval_merger.py`: `merge_intervals(intervals: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> list[tuple[int, int]]` which merges overlapping or adjacent closed intervals `[start, end]` where touching intervals (`a_end == b_start`) are merged into a single continuous interval, and `total_covered_duration(intervals: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> int` which returns the total covered length across the merged intervals.
entry_points: def merge_intervals(intervals: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
edge_cases: Empty input list returns [] for merge_intervals and 0 for total_covered_duration
Raise ValueError if any interval has start > end
Touching intervals like (1, 5) and (5, 8) must be merged into (1, 8)
Unsorted input intervals must be sorted before merging

constraints.time_complexity: O(N log N) due to sorting where N is number of intervals
constraints.space_complexity: O(N) to store the merged output

acceptance_tests.description: Merges unsorted overlapping and adjacent intervals properly.
acceptance_tests.test_code:
def test_overlapping_and_adjacent_merge():
    raw = [(10, 15), (1, 3), (3, 6), (8, 12)]
    assert merge_intervals(raw) == [(1, 6), (8, 15)]
    assert total_covered_duration(raw) == (6 - 1) + (15 - 8)

acceptance_tests.description: Handles empty lists and point intervals (start == end).
acceptance_tests.test_code:
def test_empty_and_zero_length_intervals():
    assert merge_intervals([]) == []
    assert total_covered_duration([]) == 0
    assert merge_intervals([(4, 4), (4, 7)]) == [(4, 7)]
    assert total_covered_duration([(4, 4)]) == 0
